                    ### Question
                    A 58-year-old woman presents to the physician for a routine gynecological visit. She denies any acute issues and remarks that she has not been sexually active for the past year. Her last Pap test was negative for any abnormal cytology. A pelvic examination and Pap test is performed at the current visit with no remarkable findings. Which of the following approaches to cervical cancer screening is most appropriate for this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Colposcopy at the current visit to verify Pap test results
opb. Colposcopy in 3 years
opc. Discontinue screening until the patient becomes sexually active
opd. Pap test and HPV test in 5 years
ope. Pap test only in 5 years

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient is 58 years old and has had a negative Pap test. Current guidelines from the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) recommend that women aged 30-65 should undergo Pap and HPV co-testing every 5 years or Pap testing alone every 3 years. Since the patient has no acute issues and has not been sexually active, discontinuing screening is not recommended. Colposcopy is not indicated with negative Pap results. Therefore, the most appropriate approach for cervical cancer screening for this patient is to perform Pap and HPV testing in 5 years, aligning with the consensus guidelines.
